materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Walk-through of one ES futures trade across 10 numbered steps plus a closing multi-timeframe summary. Key semantics for the false-breakout/range-reversion family: (step 6) the market bounces but does not expand TICK distribution, volume, or volume at the offer; the 13:39 bar highs are declared 'candidate highs' and the market is viewed as in a trading range defined by the 13:30 lows and the 13:39 highs; (step 7) 'I sell when we make positive TICK readings and green Market Delta readings (more volume at offer than bid) that cannot make fresh price highs... My stop is above the 13:39 highs--a move to new highs invalidates my idea. My profit target is the lows of the trading range.'; (step 9) enter after a short-term candidate high as close to that high as possible, play for the highest-probability move (return to the bottom of the range), not a home run breakout; 'If the market moves into breakout mode, I'll consider that a separate trade and setup.'; closing: the pattern occurs on multiple time frames; focus on 1) market's general direction, 2) presence of a trading range, 3) a candidate price high or low, 4) an entry leaning on that candidate, 5) a high probability price target. Uses NYSE TICK and Market Delta (bid/offer volume).
materials.content_type: official blog post (step-by-step trade walk-through; ES futures)
materials.diversity_role: candidate highs / trading range / invalidation / target / entry trigger / no-trade / applicability

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Classifies most trading patterns into three basic setups: 1) Reversal trades ('The market moves to or just beyond the edges of a trading range (a consolidation area, the value area from the prior day), cannot sustain buying/selling interest, and falls back into that range. The initial target... will generally be the midpoint of that range (which may also be the pivot level from the previous day or week); a reversal on good volume and very weak/strong NYSE TICK will frequently test the opposite end of that range'); 2) Breakout trades (range-bound market surges out on enhanced volume + very high/low NYSE TICK; usually a catalyst; cross-market repricing as confirmation; initial targets R1/R2/R3, S1/S2/S3); 3) Continuation trades (trend in place, wait for pullback; volume expands with trend and contracts on pullbacks; trending cumulative NYSE TICK and Market Delta; TICK/Delta pullbacks as entries).
materials.content_type: official blog post (setup taxonomy: reversal / breakout / continuation)
materials.diversity_role: reversal/breakout/continuation separation; range-edge / value-area; target conventions; confirmation

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Short post using a range-day read in ES futures. Covers: 'we came into the day sensitive to it being a range day and saw that the important XLE and XLF sectors were not confirming the upside breakout. Also looking sketchy at the highs were XLB and XLV.' Then: 'Unable to take out yesterday's high, we moved back into the morning range (bottom chart). Note how you didn't need to catch the exact top to recognize that the upmove was failing and play a reversion back to VWAP as a first target.' Closing process claim: 'Making the hard trade: It's all about preparation.' Key semantics: prior-day high, morning range, range-day call, sector non-confirmation, reversion-to-VWAP target, no need to catch the exact top.
materials.content_type: official blog post (failed-breakout / range-day market read; ES futures + sector confirmation)
materials.diversity_role: failed prior-day-high breakout; morning range; reversion to VWAP; sector non-confirmation; invalidation

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Defines a false breakout: 'A false breakout occurs when we get new highs or lows following an extended trading range, only to see trade return to that range. These occur at every time frame.' The example short-term false break to the downside in ES was 'not confirmed by fresh lows for the NASDAQ or Russell averages--often a nice tell for false breaks.' Trading consequence: 'a fade back into the day's range is generally a great play for a move back to the VWAP. On sustained strength, those false breaks lead to a complete rotation through the range to the opposite extreme.' Uses a Market Delta chart.
materials.content_type: official blog post (false-breakout definition and trade; ES + Market Delta + cross-index tell)
materials.diversity_role: false-breakout definition; return-to-range; reversion-to-VWAP; cross-index non-confirmation

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.canonical_title: Trading Patterns: Failed Opening Range Breakout
materials.content_note: Annotated chart of Russell 2000 (ER2) futures with NYSE TICK and volume for the morning of 2007-06-01. 'The preopening and opening ranges are extremely important, because they locate the market's estimate of value.' 'If we get a breakout from the preopening range on expanded volume and strong NYSE TICK, it means that the market is undergoing a new valuation ... The key principle... is that, if this revaluation is genuine, we should not return to the prior trading range.' A momentum (volume) peak, subsequent price peak on reduced upside momentum but very strong TICK, then failure of positive TICK readings to achieve new highs => 'failed opening range breakout in the making. Knowing that, we can anticipate a move back to the midpoint of that opening range; i.e., a return to the prior level of valuation.' 'Notice how the chart above integrates a number of market dynamics over time: valuation levels, volume, TICK, and price.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (failed opening-range breakout; Russell 2000 ER2 futures + NYSE TICK + volume)
materials.diversity_role: opening-range boundary; genuine-breakout condition; failed-breakout condition; midpoint target; TICK/volume integration

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.canonical_title: The Relevance of VWAP in a Range Market
materials.content_note: 'The volume-weighted average price (VWAP; red line above) is an excellent reference point in range bound markets. In a good range trade, we'll tend to see a narrow value area (volume will be transacted within a narrow price band) and moves away from value will tend to return back to (and usually through) VWAP. In a true range trade, we'll also see little slope to VWAP, as we transact volume relatively evenly above and below that average price.' 'If you're playing for a range breakout, it often makes sense to track the distribution of NYSE TICK, Cumulative Delta, and intermarket themes. Often we'll see buying or selling unable to pierce VWAP prior to a breakout to the downside or upside. It's the inability of price to trade through VWAP that shows buying or selling drying up.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (VWAP reference point in range markets; ES)
materials.diversity_role: VWAP definition; return-to-VWAP; range-breakout handicap via TICK/Cumulative Delta/intermarket

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.canonical_title: Notes on Trading a Range Market
materials.content_note: 'By making the call of range day, we are prepared to fade moves away from the day's volume-weighted average price. We can also then focus on how markets trade above and below VWAP to handicap the odds of a breakout from the trading range.' 'As a rough rule, I look for the amplitudes of moves above and below VWAP in a range market to be similar: If we trade two points above VWAP before retreating, I'll look for a reversal move to travel two points below VWAP. Focusing on that rule can be helpful in identifying range extensions that become range breakouts.' Note: the 'two points' amplitude is an example-specific rough rule, not a pinned universal threshold.
materials.content_type: official blog post (range-day fade rule; rough VWAP-amplitude symmetry rule; ES)
materials.diversity_role: range-day call; fade-away-from-VWAP; VWAP-amplitude rough rule; breakout handicap

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: Very simple real-time template: '1) Market opens above or below the previous day's pivot on low volume and relatively narrow breadth and TICK: Play for a move back to pivot and consider a range day, with moves oscillating around VWAP; 2) Market makes a good move on strong/weak TICK and average or above volume early in the AM and holds above/below pivot on next pullback: Play for a move to the overnight high/low and/or the previous day's high/low; 3) ... on strong/weak TICK and average or better volume: Play for a move to previous day's high/low and R1/S1; 4) ... Play for a move to R2/S2.' 'If you are playing a range market, you should fade moves away from VWAP that cannot sustain upside/downside price targets.' 'If you are playing for a directional move up/down, price should stay above/below the day's VWAP.' Note: template mixes price levels with breadth and TICK conditions.
materials.content_type: official blog post (intraday trading template; pivot/overnight/VWAP price levels; breadth + TICK)
materials.diversity_role: range-day template; fade-away-from-VWAP; pivot/overnight/prior-day-high reference levels; TICK+breadth

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.canonical_title: Breakouts From Trading Ranges: Making the Identification
materials.content_note: Identifies genuine range breakouts: legit breakout => traders jump aboard + counter-positioned bail out => 'creates enhanced volume on the breakout move.' 'The key, then, is recognizing when a breakout is a genuine one and when it is false. Markets can move out of their ranges, only to fail to attract volume/participation and fall back toward their volume-weighted averages (i.e., their previous estimates of value).' Other than volume expansion, features of range breakouts: '1) Sectors that have been leading the market should lead the market in the direction of the break; 2) The vast majority of sectors should participate in the break, expanding the plurality of advancing or declining stocks; 3) The market should stay below its volume-weighted average price ... as it searches for new, lower levels of value; 4) ... similar revaluations among related asset classes, such as Treasury instruments, commodities, and currencies.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (genuine vs false breakout identification; volume + sector + breadth + VWAP + cross-asset)
materials.diversity_role: genuine-vs-false breakout identification; enhanced volume; sector participation; VWAP; cross-asset revaluation

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.content_note: 'Day structure, for me as an intraday trader, trumps longer timeframe trend considerations.' Seven day-structure possibilities: 1) Range Day (oscillate around an average price value, relatively low volatility, likely ending not far from its opening price level and/or VWAP); 2) Upside Trend Day; 3) Downside Trend Day; 4) Upside Breakout Day (opens within a range, builds volume and participation at the upper end, price breaks above the range, further acceptance with solid volume); 5) Downside Breakout Day; 6) False Upside Breakout Day ('The market opens within a range and moves above the range, usually with limited participation and volume that wanes with higher prices, only to fall back into the range and return toward VWAP. A false upside breakout represents an extension of range trading conditions.'); 7) False Downside Breakout Day. 'In range markets and on false breakouts, you'll be trading for moves toward VWAP and often the prior day's pivot level. In trending and breakout markets, you'll be trading for moves away from VWAP and toward the R1/R2/R3 or S1/S2/S3 price levels. In other words, you'll be fading price strength and weakness in range and false breakout markets and trading with strength and weakness during trending and breakout conditions.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (seven day-structure types; range/false-breakout trading toward VWAP)
materials.diversity_role: day-structure taxonomy; range day; false upside/downside breakout day; trading toward vs away from VWAP

materials.author: Brett N. Steenbarger, Ph.D.
materials.canonical_title: Anatomy of a False Breakout in the Stock Market
materials.content_note: Annotated chart of the Russell 2000 (ER2) futures afternoon trade. 'For the better part of an hour, we're trading in a range, but the distribution of the NYSE TICK during that range was positive. We then break out of the range on enhanced volume, as buyers lift offers.' The time-trend pattern triggered on 14 of the last 16 bars closing higher; 'From that point forward, thrusts in the NYSE TICK above 1000 are no longer able to generate higher prices; there is a stalling out of the rally. This emboldens the sellers, who proceed to take the market back to the midpoint of the prior trading range.' Opposite time-trend pattern on enhanced volume (16 of prior 19 bars closing lower). 'Much of the market's short-term swings consists of counter-movement once markets become too one-sided.'
materials.content_type: official blog post (false breakout anatomy; Russell 2000 ER2 futures + NYSE TICK + volume)
materials.diversity_role: false-breakout anatomy; TICK thrust failure; return to range midpoint; enhanced-volume breakout
